description: Task cost attribution in detail page + Workflow breadcrumb in task detail + Agent Manifest runtime validation (Hermes Profile online probe during operations-health).
steps: In apps/ajun-runtime/src/task-record-service.ts, extend the detail() method to include a 'costAttribution' field when returning a task record. Query task usage data (from task.usage which uses the task-usage.ts recordTaskUsage schema) to build: totalCostDisplay (formatted string), modelInputTokens, modelOutputTokens, durationMs, executor. The data already exists in task.usage per the recordTaskUsage function - just project it into the detail response.

In frontend/src/task-record-detail-view.ts, add a renderCostSection(detail) function that renders a section 'This cost' showing: executor agent name, duration, token counts, total cost. Use the html tagged template. Render it after the main task detail content. Only show if costAttribution has data.

In apps/ajun-runtime/src/task-record-service.ts detail(), also include workflow breadcrumb data: parentWorkflowId (from task.workflow.parentWorkflowId or parent ref), current workflowId + stepId, childTaskIds (query store for tasks with workflow.parentWorkflowId matching current). Return as 'workflowBreadcrumb' field.

In frontend/src/task-record-detail-view.ts, add a renderWorkflowBreadcrumb(detail) function that renders a breadcrumb navigation showing parent > current > children links. Each item shows taskId (short ref) and title. Use the html tagged template.

For Agent Manifest runtime validation: In apps/ajun-runtime/src/agent-manifest-health-probe.ts, create a probe function that takes a list of active agent manifests and the LocalAiCapabilityClient, then for each agent checks if its Hermes Profile is online by doing a read-only probe to the local AI gateway health endpoint (GET /health on port 18082). Map the result to update capability status (reachable vs configured). This is a pure read-only probe.

Integrate the agent manifest probe into the operations-health flow: In paperclip-heartbeat.ts or deterministic-local-health-probe.ts, call the probe during health checks and include results in the health overview response.

Write test in apps/ajun-runtime/test/task-cost-attribution.test.js verifying: (1) detail response includes costAttribution when task has usage data, (2) costAttribution has expected fields, (3) missing usage returns null costAttribution.

Write test in apps/ajun-runtime/test/workflow-breadcrumb.test.js verifying: (1) detail includes workflowBreadcrumb when task has workflow data, (2) breadcrumb contains parent/current/children structure, (3) no workflow data returns null.
Write test in apps/ajun-runtime/test/agent-manifest-health-probe.test.js verifying the probe returns online/offline status per agent based on mocked gateway responses.
acceptance_criteria: Task detail API response includes costAttribution with cost/token/duration data when available
Task detail API response includes workflowBreadcrumb with parent/current/children when task has workflow context
Frontend renders cost section in task detail page
Frontend renders workflow breadcrumb in task detail page
Agent manifest probe correctly checks gateway health endpoint
Probe results appear in health overview
All existing tests continue to pass
verification: npm run build:frontend --workspace=ajun-runtime && git diff --exit-code apps/ajun-runtime/public/
findings: Handler file at exactly 750 split-lines (the limit); agent health probe route merged onto same line as custom AI route. Pre-existing 3 test failures unchanged. costAttribution uses cost.amount directly (already a dollar float in task-usage normalizeCost). workflowBreadcrumb siblings exclude the current task itself.
